mainTopic: The סוטה scroll versus a גט, praise of רבי מאיר and of sharp reasoning, why הלכה follows בית הלל, and the new משנה on the width of the קורה
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ruling about a גט: a גט written for one woman cannot be used by a namesake for his own wife. The גמרא tries to apply this to the סוטה scroll, but rejects the comparison. A גט must be written for her, while for a סוטה only the doing, the erasing, must be for her. The topic then turns to praise of רבי מאיר, whose colleagues could not follow the depth of his reasoning, so the הלכה was not fixed like him. The גמרא also explains his name and the name נהוראי, describes how רבי was sharpened by seeing him, and tells of sharp students who could argue both sides, including רבינא's קל וחומר about a שרץ, which is rejected. Next comes the famous בת קול: both בית שמאי and בית הלל speak 'the words of the living God,' but the הלכה follows בית הלל because of their humility, shown by a משנה about סוכה. The aggadah closes with their debate over whether man should have been created, ending with a call to examine one's deeds. Finally, a new משנה begins the laws of the קורה over a מבוי: how wide and strong it must be, and how to judge curved and round beams.

steps.title: A divorce document written for one woman cannot be used by a namesake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a ruling about a גט: a man wrote one for his wife and changed his mind. A neighbor with the same name and a wife with the same name may not use it. This is brought to show that a סוטה scroll written for one woman cannot be used for another.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and he changed his mind, and a man from his town found him and said: 'Your name is like my name, and your wife's name is like my wife's name.' The document is invalid for divorcing with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes a quoted ruling about a גט to make a comparison: just as a גט must be written specifically for one woman, so too a סוטה scroll should need to be written specifically for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is built so that every detail matches: same husband's name, same wife's name, same town. The גט is still invalid, because it was not written for this second woman. The גמרא wants to carry this 'must be written for her' rule over to the סוטה scroll.
steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a quoted source. The words 'and he changed his mind' continue a ruling that begins earlier: a man who wrote a גט to divorce his wife. Nobody new is speaking here.

phrases.english: and he changed his mind, and a man from his town found him
phrases.notes: The husband who wrote the גט decided not to divorce his wife.

phrases.english: and said: Your name is like my name
and your wife's name is like my wife's name
phrases.notes: So the written text would fit him exactly.

phrases.english: it is invalid to divorce with it!
phrases.notes: The document was not written for his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִמְלַךְ וּמְצָאוֹ בֶּן עִירוֹ וְאָמַר: שִׁמְךָ כִּשְׁמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a citation that began on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: That a סוטה scroll written for one woman cannot be used for another.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that a גט written for one woman is invalid for a namesake's wife.

steps.title: The comparison fails because the verses require different things
steps.stepSummary: For a גט the verse says 'he shall write for her,' so the writing must be for her. For a סוטה the verse says 'he shall do for her,' so only the doing must be for her, and that doing is the erasing.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? There it is written 'and he shall write for her,' so we need writing for her sake. Here it is written 'and he shall do to her,' so we need the doing for her sake, and her 'doing' is the erasing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the גט by pointing to the different wording of each verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'for her' is attached to a different action in each case. For a גט, 'for her' is attached to writing, so the writing must be for her. For a סוטה, 'for her' is attached to doing, and the key action done for her is erasing the scroll into the water, so the writing itself does not need to be for her.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)
'and he shall write for her' (the verse about a גט)
'and he shall do to her' (the verse about a סוטה)
for her sake, specifically for her

steps.whatToRemember: A גט must be written for the specific woman. For a סוטה, only the erasing must be done for her, so the scroll's writing is not tied to one woman.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common way the גמרא reads verses: the phrase 'for her' applies only to the specific action the verse mentions.

phrases.english: How can you compare?
phrases.notes: Signals rejection.

phrases.english: There, 'and he shall write for her' is written
phrases.notes: Deuteronomy 24:1, about a גט.

phrases.english: so we require writing for her sake
here, 'and he shall do to her' is written
phrases.notes: Numbers 5:30, about a סוטה.

phrases.english: so we require the doing for her sake
and her 'doing' is the erasure.
phrases.notes: Only the erasing must be for her, not the writing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between a גט and a סוטה scroll.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verses require 'for her' for different actions: writing in a גט, but doing (erasure) in a סוטה.

steps.title: Why the law does not follow the unmatched genius of his generation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר חנינא says no one in רבי מאיר's generation was his equal. Still, the הלכה was not set like him, because his colleagues could not fully grasp his reasoning. He could argue convincingly for either side of an issue.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר חנינא said: It is revealed and known before the One who spoke and the world came to be that there was no one in רבי מאיר's generation like him. So why didn't they fix the הלכה like him? Because his colleagues could not reach the depth of his thinking. He would say about something impure that it is pure and show a reason for it, and about something pure that it is impure and show a reason for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the halachic topic to praising רבי מאיר, who was mentioned in the earlier discussion. It explains why the הלכה usually does not follow him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement asks its own question and answers it. If רבי מאיר was the greatest, why not follow him? Because he could build a strong argument for either side, his colleagues could not tell when he meant a ruling as final and when he was sharpening the debate. So they could not rely on his rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: the One who spoke and the world came to be (God)
the full depth of his thinking
shows a reason or justification for it

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not being criticized. The הלכה does not follow him because of his brilliance, not because of a flaw in him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the classic reason why, in many disputes, the הלכה does not follow רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said:
It is revealed and known before
the One who spoke and the world came to be
phrases.notes: God.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר כְּמוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: that there was no one in Rabbi Meir's generation like him

phrases.aramaic: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא קָבְעוּ הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ?
phrases.english: So why didn't they fix the law like him?
Because his colleagues were not able
to reach the full depth of his thinking.
For he would say about something impure that it is pure
and show a reason for it,
about something pure that it is impure
and show a reason for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from הלכה to praise of רבי מאיר, who appeared in the earlier discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר was unmatched, but the הלכה was not fixed like him because his colleagues could not grasp the depth of his reasoning.

steps.title: The real name of the sage called the 'one who lights up'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that רבי מאיר's real name was רבי נהוראי. He was called מאיר ('the one who lights up') because he lit up the eyes of the sages in הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי מאיר was not his name. Rather, רבי נהוראי was his name. Why was he called רבי מאיר? Because he lights up the eyes of the sages in הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues praising רבי מאיר by quoting a ברייתא that explains his name as a title of honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מאיר' means 'lights up.' According to the ברייתא, it was a description of what he did, clarifying הלכה for other scholars, rather than his birth name.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir was not his name
rather, Rabbi Nehorai was his name
And why was he called Rabbi Meir?
Because he lights up the eyes of the sages in הלכה.
phrases.notes: A play on the word מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues praising רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר's real name was רבי נהוראי. 'מאיר' was a title for his clarifying of הלכה.

steps.title: The sage known as נהוראי was really someone else
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the תנא known as רבי נהוראי was really רבי נחמיה, or according to others רבי אלעזר בן ערך. He was called נהוראי because he enlightened the eyes of the sages in הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And נהוראי was not his name. Rather, רבי נחמיה was his name, and some say רבי אלעזר בן ערך was his name. Why was he called נהוראי? Because he enlightens the eyes of the sages in הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains that the תנא known as רבי נהוראי also carried a title rather than his birth name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different sage from רבי מאיר: the separate תנא known by the name רבי נהוראי. Two opinions are given for his real identity, and his title 'נהוראי' is also explained as 'giving light.'

keyTerms.meaning: a leading student of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי

steps.whatToRemember: Both 'מאיר' and 'נהוראי' are titles that mean 'giving light,' because these sages clarified הלכה for others.
steps.confusionAlert: 'נהוראי' in this step is not רבי מאיר. It refers to the separate תנא commonly called רבי נהוראי.

phrases.english: And Nehorai was not his name
phrases.notes: Refers to the separate תנא known as רבי נהוראי.

phrases.english: rather, Rabbi Nechemya was his name

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ שְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Elazar ben Arach was his name
And why was he called Nehorai?
Because he enlightens the eyes of the sages in הלכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא נְהוֹרַאי שְׁמוֹ אֶלָּא רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה שְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second name explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא called נהוראי was רבי נחמיה, or according to others רבי אלעזר בן ערך. He was named for enlightening the sages.

steps.title: רבי became sharp just from seeing רבי מאיר from behind
steps.stepSummary: רבי says he is sharper than his colleagues because he saw רבי מאיר from behind. Had he seen him from the front, he would be sharper still, based on the פסוק 'your eyes shall see your teacher.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: The reason I am sharper than my colleagues is that I saw רבי מאיר from behind. If I had seen him from the front, I would be even sharper. As the פסוק says: 'And your eyes shall see your teacher.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another praise of רבי מאיר, this time from his own student רבי. Even sitting behind רבי מאיר made רבי sharper than everyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the earlier claim that no one in רבי מאיר's generation was his equal. רבי teaches that just seeing a great teacher sharpens the mind. He uses the פסוק in ישעיהו to show that seeing the teacher's face is the ideal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the value of learning in front of a רבי, face to face, and not just from a distance or from books.

phrases.english: Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) said:
The fact that I am sharper than my colleagues
is because I saw Rabbi Meir from behind,
phrases.notes: He sat behind רבי מאיר in the study hall.

phrases.english: and had I seen him from the front,
I would have been even sharper —
as it is written: “And your eyes shall see your teacher.”
phrases.notes: ישעיהו ל:כ

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of statements praising רבי מאיר's greatness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing a great teacher, especially face to face, sharpens a student's mind.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's student סומכוס gave 48 reasons for each side
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that רבי מאיר had a student named סומכוס who could give 48 reasons for טומאה and 48 reasons for טהרה on every single topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי מאיר had a student named סומכוס. On every topic of טומאה he could give 48 reasons why it is טמא, and on every topic of טהרה he could give 48 reasons why it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how strong רבי מאיר's school was by describing his student סומכוס. He could build 48 arguments for either side of any purity question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said רבי מאיר could argue convincingly for both sides of an issue. Here we see that same skill in his student, on a huge scale. The point is mental sharpness, not that each of these reasons was the final הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rabbi Meir had a student
and his name was Sumchus,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר עַל כׇּל דָּבָר וְדָבָר שֶׁל טוּמְאָה
phrases.english: who would say, about each and every matter of impurity,
forty-eight reasons for impurity,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל כׇּל דָּבָר וְדָבָר שֶׁל טׇהֳרָה
phrases.english: and about each and every matter of purity
forty-eight reasons for purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: תַּלְמִיד הָיָה לוֹ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְסוֹמְכוֹס שְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי מאיר himself to his student, showing the same two-sided brilliance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סומכוס, student of רבי מאיר, could give 48 reasons for each side of every טומאה and טהרה question.

steps.title: A student in יבנה could argue 150 ways that a שרץ is pure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a distinguished student in יבנה could give 150 reasons to declare a שרץ טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: There was a distinguished student in יבנה who could declare a שרץ טהור with 150 reasons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with an even bigger example of sharp reasoning. A student could find 150 arguments that a שרץ is pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is more striking than סומכוס, because the תורה clearly says a שרץ is טמא. The student was not changing the הלכה. He was showing how far a sharp mind can push logical arguments.

keyTerms.meaning: the city of the great academy
creeping animal that the תורה declares impure

steps.confusionAlert: The שרץ remains טמא! The תורה says so explicitly. These 150 reasons were an exercise in sharpness, not a real ruling that a שרץ is pure.

phrases.english: It was taught: There was a distinguished student in Yavneh
who could declare the creeping animal pure
with one hundred and fifty reasons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the example from 48 reasons on each side to 150 reasons for purifying something the תורה calls impure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sharp student in יבנה could build 150 arguments that a שרץ is טהור.

steps.title: רבינא's own argument that a creeping animal should be pure
steps.stepSummary: רבינא offers his own קל וחומר: a snake kills and so creates more טומאה, yet it is טהור. A שרץ does not kill, so all the more so it should be טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: I too will reason and declare it pure. A snake kills, and so it adds טומאה to the world (by making dead bodies), and yet a snake is טהור. A שרץ does not kill and does not add טומאה, so isn't it all the more so טהור?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a sample of the kind of argument the יבנה student might have used. He builds a קל וחומר comparing a snake to a שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A snake causes deaths, and a dead body is the strongest source of טומאה, yet a snake itself does not make things טמא. A שרץ causes no deaths, so logically it should be even 'more pure.' This shows how logic alone can seem to defeat a clear פסוק, which is exactly the kind of sharp exercise the גמרא is describing.

keyTerms.meaning: all the more so (a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא praises רבי מאיר, his student סומכוס (48 reasons each way), and then other sharp minds, such as the יבנה student with 150 reasons for purifying a שרץ and רבינא's sample קל וחומר from a snake. The הלכה itself does not change. The שרץ stays טמא, and the next step rejects רבינא's argument.

phrases.english: Ravina said: I will reason and declare it pure:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה נָחָשׁ שֶׁמֵּמִית וּמַרְבֶּה טוּמְאָה — טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: If a snake, which kills and so increases impurity, is pure,
phrases.notes: By killing, the snake creates corpses, which are a severe source of טומאה.

phrases.english: then a creeping animal, which does not kill and increase impurity,
all the more so should it be pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete example of the kind of reasoning the יבנה student used to purify a שרץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קל וחומר from a snake (which kills yet is טהור) to a שרץ (which does not kill) appears to make the שרץ טהור, as an exercise in sharp reasoning.

steps.title: The snake argument is rejected: a snake is like a thorn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבינא's קל וחומר. A snake that kills is just acting like a thorn, and a thorn causes harm without being טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not correct. A snake is only doing what a thorn does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against רבינא's קל וחומר from the previous step and says it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא argued that a snake causes death, and therefore more טומאה, yet it is טהור. So a שרץ, which does not kill, should surely be טהור too. The גמרא answers that a snake kills the way a thorn injures: it is a physical object causing harm. Causing death does not tell us anything about whether the creature itself is טמא, so the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so (a rejection formula)

phrases.english: But it is not so —
it is merely doing the act of a thorn.
phrases.notes: A thorn can injure or kill, yet it is not טמא. The snake is the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבינא's קל וחומר from Step 9.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The snake's ability to kill is just physical harm, like a thorn. It has no connection to whether the creature is טמא.

steps.title: A Heavenly voice: both views are divine, but the law follows בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: שמואל reports that בית שמאי and בית הלל argued for three years. A בת קול declared that both views are 'the words of the living God,' but the הלכה follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of שמואל: For three years בית שמאי and בית הלל argued. Each side said, 'The law follows us.' Then a Heavenly voice came out and said: 'Both these and those are the words of the living God, and the law follows בית הלל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a famous teaching about how the long dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל was finally settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side insisted that the practical law should follow its own view. The בת קול did two things at once. It confirmed that both opinions are true Torah, and it ruled that in practice we follow בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of the students of שמאי
The school of the students of הלל
Both these and those are the words of the living God

steps.confusionAlert: 'Both are the words of the living God' does NOT mean you may follow either view in practice. The same בת קול ruled that the practical הלכה follows בית הלל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that the הלכה follows בית הלל. It also teaches that a rejected opinion can still be genuine Torah.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Shmuel said:
For three years they disagreed,
Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.
These said: The law follows us,
and those said: The law follows us.
A Heavenly voice came out and said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים הֵן,
phrases.english: These and those are the words of the living God,
and the law follows Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, following the earlier discussion of sharp scholars and why the הלכה does not follow them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both views are divine truth, but the practical הלכה follows בית הלל.

steps.title: If both views are true, why did בית הלל win?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if both views are 'the words of the living God,' why did בית הלל earn the right to have the law follow them?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since both these and those are the words of the living God, why did בית הלל merit having the law set according to their view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks an obvious question about the בת קול it just quoted. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both sides are equally true Torah, truth alone cannot be the reason for choosing בית הלל. So the גמרא wants to know what made them deserve to set the practical law.

phrases.english: But since these and those
are the words of the living God,
why did Beit Hillel merit
to have the law set according to them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים מִפְּנֵי מָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the בת קול's ruling in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What made בית הלל worthy of setting the practical law, if both views are true?

steps.title: Because בית הלל were gentle, humble, and quoted בית שמאי first
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל were gentle and patient when insulted. They taught בית שמאי's view along with their own, and they even said בית שמאי's view first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they were gentle and humble. They taught their own words and the words of בית שמאי. And more than that, they said the words of בית שמאי before their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. בית הלל earned the right to set the law because of their good character and their respect for the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is about character, not about who was right. There are three points, each going one step further. First, בית הלל were gentle and patient. Second, they taught בית שמאי's opinion too. Third, they mentioned בית שמאי's opinion before their own.

keyTerms.meaning: They put first; they give priority

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל did not win because they were 'more right.' They won because they were humble and respected their opponents, even saying בית שמאי's view first.

phrases.english: Because they were gentle and patient when insulted,
and they taught their own words and the words of Beit Shammai,
and not only that, but
they put the words of Beit Shammai before their own words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית הלל earned the right to set the law through humility, by teaching בית שמאי's view, and by stating it before their own.

steps.title: An example from the משנה: eating in a סוכה with the table in the house
steps.stepSummary: To show how בית הלל put בית שמאי first, the גמרא brings a משנה. In it, בית שמאי say a person sitting with his head and most of his body in the סוכה, but his table in the house, has not fulfilled the מצוה‎. בית הלל say he has.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If a person had his head and most of his body in the סוכה, and his table inside the house, בית שמאי say it is invalid and בית הלל say it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins an example to prove the last point, that בית הלל mentioned בית שמאי first. This step sets up the case, and the actual proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling itself is not the point here. The גמרא quotes this משנה because of how בית הלל tell the story that follows in it. This step just sets out the basic dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: His head and most of his body

phrases.english: As that which we learned:
One whose head and most of his body were in the sukka
and his table was inside the house:
Beit Shammai rule it invalid,
and Beit Hillel rule it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an example to illustrate the claim in Step 13 that בית הלל put בית שמאי first.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that בית הלל mentioned בית שמאי before themselves.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת סוכה about a person whose table is in the house.

steps.title: בית הלל's story, naming the elders of בית שמאי first
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל bring a story as proof. The elders of both schools visited רבי יוחנן בן החורנית and found him sitting with his head and most of his body in the סוכה and his table in the house. בית הלל name the elders of בית שמאי before their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: Didn't it happen that the elders of בית שמאי and the elders of בית הלל went to visit רבי יוחנן בן החורנית, and they found him sitting with his head and most of his body in the סוכה and his table inside the house?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the משנה, בית הלל bring a real-life story to support their view. The גמרא's point is the order of names: בית הלל mention 'the elders of בית שמאי' first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית הלל's argument is that the elders saw this and did not object. For our גמרא, what matters is that בית הלל are telling the story to prove their own view, yet they still name their opponents first. This is the clear example of 'they put the words of בית שמאי first.'

keyTerms.meaning: A sage whom both schools visited

steps.confusionAlert: Our גמרא is not quoting this story to decide the הלכה of סוכה. It quotes it to show that בית הלל named בית שמאי first, even in their own proof.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
Wasn't there such an incident,
that the elders of Beit Shammai went
phrases.notes: This is the key detail: בית שמאי are named first.

phrases.english: and the elders of Beit Hillel

phrases.aramaic: לְבַקֵּר אֶת רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן הַחוֹרָנִית
phrases.english: to visit Rabbi Yochanan ben HaChoranit,
and they found him sitting
with his head and most of his body in the sukka
and his table inside the house?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי לֹא כָּךְ הָיָה מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from Step 14 with בית הלל's proof story.
steps.raayaObject: Inside the משנה: בית הלל's view that the סוכה is valid. For our גמרא: the claim that בית הלל put בית שמאי first.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident with רבי יוחנן בן החורנית, told with the elders of בית שמאי named first.

steps.title: בית שמאי reject the story: the elders told him he never fulfilled the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that the story is no proof. The elders actually told רבי יוחנן בן החורנית that if this was his practice, he had never fulfilled the מצוה of סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: Is that a proof? They also told him: If you used to act this way, you have never fulfilled the מצוה of סוכה in your whole life.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push back on בית הלל's story. They say the elders actually criticized רבי יוחנן בן החורנית, so the story supports their view instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל used the story to show that the elders approved. בית שמאי reply that the elders, at least those of בית שמאי, objected and told him he had never fulfilled the מצוה. This closes the quoted משנה. For our גמרא, the important detail has already been shown in the previous step.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? (rejecting a proof)
Used to act; had the practice
The מצוה of dwelling in a סוכה

steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה is brought to show one thing: even when בית הלל argue for their own view, they say 'the elders of בית שמאי' first. This humility is why the הלכה follows them.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:
Is there a proof from there?!
They too said to him:
If this is how you used to act,
you have never fulfilled the מצוה of sukka in all your days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אִי מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בית שמאי reject בית הלל's proof story from Step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: בית הלל's proof from the incident with רבי יוחנן בן החורנית.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The elders did not approve. They told him he had never fulfilled the מצוה.

steps.title: The lesson: whoever lowers himself is raised up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that בית הלל's success teaches a general rule. God lifts up the humble and lowers the arrogant. Greatness runs from those who chase it and chases those who run from it. Whoever forces the moment is pushed back by it, and whoever yields to the moment has it stand by him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches you that anyone who lowers himself, God raises him up, and anyone who raises himself, God lowers him. Anyone who chases greatness, greatness runs away from him. Anyone who runs away from greatness, greatness chases after him. Anyone who pushes the moment, the moment pushes him back. Anyone who steps back for the moment, the moment stands by him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes its explanation of why הלכה follows בית הלל. It turns their humility into a lesson for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 13, the גמרא said בית הלל won because they were humble and even quoted בית שמאי first. Now it widens that point into a rule of life. Being humble did not make בית הלל lose. It is exactly what made them win.

keyTerms.meaning: to teach you; introduces the lesson drawn from what came before
one who forces the moment, insisting things happen exactly when he wants

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל earned the right to have הלכה follow them because of their humility. The גמרא makes this a general rule: lowering yourself leads to being raised up.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why הלכה follows בית הלל even though both views are 'אלו ואלו דברי אלהים חיים.' The deciding factor was their character, not only their reasoning.

phrases.english: To teach you that anyone who lowers himself —
phrases.notes: Connects back to בית הלל's humility from step 13.

phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, raises him up,
and anyone who raises himself up —
the Holy One, Blessed be He, lowers him.
Anyone who chases after greatness —
greatness runs away from him,
and anyone who runs away from greatness —
greatness chases after him,
and anyone who pushes the moment —
phrases.notes: Insisting on getting something exactly when he wants it.

phrases.english: the moment pushes him back,
and anyone who steps back for the moment —
phrases.notes: Someone who is patient and waits.

phrases.english: the moment stands by him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the section on why הלכה follows בית הלל by drawing a moral lesson from their humility.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Humility brings success. God raises the humble and lowers the arrogant, and greatness comes to those who do not chase it.

steps.title: The long debate over whether man should have been created
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that בית שמאי and בית הלל argued for two and a half years. One side said it would be better for man never to have been created. The other side said it is better that he was created.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: For two and a half years בית שמאי and בית הלל argued. These said: it would be better for a person not to have been created than to have been created. And those said: it is better for a person to have been created than not to have been created.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about another argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל. This step lays out the two sides. The next step gives the result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike their usual practical arguments, this one is about the value of human existence itself. The ברייתא does not say which school held which view. It only says 'these' and 'those.'

keyTerms.meaning: the Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא
it is better (more comfortable) for a person

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume which school said which view. The ברייתא deliberately says only 'הללו' (these) and 'הללו' (those).

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
For two and a half years
Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagreed.
These say:
It is better for a person not to have been created
than to have been created,
and those say:
It is better for a person to have been created
than not to have been created.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים וּמֶחֱצָה נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another ברייתא about בית שמאי and בית הלל, continuing the theme of their disputes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two sides argued for years over whether it is better for man to have been created or not.

steps.title: The vote and the practical lesson: examine your deeds
steps.stepSummary: They voted and concluded that it would have been better for man not to be created. But since he has been created, he should examine his past deeds. Another version says he should carefully weigh his future deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: They counted votes and concluded: it would be better for a person not to have been created than to have been created. Now that he has been created, he should examine his deeds. And some say: he should carefully consider his deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The debate from the previous step is settled by a vote. The גמרא then turns the conclusion into practical advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The conclusion is not a reason for despair. Life carries a heavy responsibility, so a person must take his actions seriously. The two versions differ: 'יפשפש' means reviewing what you already did and fixing it. 'ימשמש' means checking what you are about to do before you do it.

keyTerms.meaning: he should examine (search through) his past deeds
and some say it this way; introduces an alternate version
he should feel out (carefully weigh) his upcoming deeds

steps.whatToRemember: Even though it would have been 'easier' not to exist, we do exist. So the job is to look honestly at our actions, both what we did and what we are about to do.
steps.confusionAlert: The conclusion does not mean life is worthless. It leads directly to a call for responsibility: since you are here, examine your deeds.

phrases.english: They counted votes and concluded:
It is better for a person not to have been created
than to have been created,
now that he has been created —
he should examine his deeds.
phrases.notes: Look back at what you did and fix it.

phrases.english: And some say:
he should carefully weigh his deeds.
phrases.notes: Think before acting on what you plan to do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the debate of step 18 by a vote and adds practical guidance.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It would have been better not to be created, but since we were, we must examine our deeds (or carefully weigh them in advance).

steps.title: How wide the cross beam must be
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה says the קורה placed over a מבוי must be wide enough to hold an אריח. An אריח is half of a three-טפחים brick. Still, a beam one טפח wide is enough, because it can hold the אריח along its width.
steps.simpleTranslation: The beam that the Sages spoke about must be wide enough to hold a small brick. A small brick is half of a brick that is three handbreadths. It is enough for the beam to be one handbreadth wide, enough to hold the small brick along its width.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the אגדה and returns to הלכה with a new משנה. It defines the minimum width of the קורה that makes a מבוי fit for carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה spoke about using a קורה to fix a מבוי. Now it gives the size. The measuring tool is an אריח, a half-brick. The משנה then says that one טפח of width is enough, even though the half-brick is a טפח and a half in one direction. The גמרא will soon discuss how this works.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
a cross beam placed over the entrance of a מבוי
a small brick, half of a full brick
a handbreadth, a basic unit of measure

steps.confusionAlert: Half of three טפחים is a טפח and a half, yet the משנה says one טפח is enough. This does not mean the beam holds the brick by a narrower side, since even the half-brick's narrow side is a טפח and a half. The משנה is saying that a one-טפח beam is enough even though the brick sticks out past it. The גמרא will explain how that works.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The beam that they (the Sages) spoke of
phrases.notes: The beam used to make a מבוי fit for carrying.

phrases.english: must be wide enough to hold a small brick.
And a small brick is half of a brick
of three handbreadths.
phrases.notes: So the half-brick measures a טפח and a half.

phrases.english: It is enough for the beam to be one handbreadth wide
enough to hold a small brick along its width.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ רְחָבָה כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל אָרִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic section and opens a new הלכה topic with a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קורה must be able to hold an אריח, and one טפח of width is enough.

steps.title: Must the beam also be sturdy? רבי יהודה disagrees
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says the קורה must be both wide enough and strong enough to hold an אריח. רבי יהודה says width alone is enough, even if it is not strong. So, for him, a beam of straw or reeds is viewed as if it were metal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It must be wide enough to hold a small brick and strong enough to hold a small brick. רבי יהודה says: wide is enough, even if it is not strong. If it was made of straw or reeds, we view it as if it were made of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second requirement, strength, and records a מחלוקת. The תנא קמא requires strength, while רבי יהודה requires only width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the beam must actually be able to bear the brick's weight. For רבי יהודה, all that matters is the measurement. That is why a flimsy beam of straw or reeds still works for him: we imagine it as strong as metal.

keyTerms.meaning: sturdy, strong enough to bear weight
we view it as if; a legal assumption

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא requires the קורה to be both wide and strong enough for an אריח. רבי יהודה requires only width, so even straw or reeds count, viewed as if they were metal.
steps.confusionAlert: The line about straw and reeds continues רבי יהודה's view. It follows from his ruling that strength does not matter. It is not the תנא קמא's opinion.

phrases.english: Wide enough to hold a small brick
and strong enough to hold a small brick.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: רְחָבָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בְּרִיאָה.
phrases.english: Wide enough, even though it is not strong.
phrases.notes: Width alone is enough.

phrases.english: If it was made of straw or of reeds —

phrases.aramaic: רוֹאִין אוֹתָהּ כְּאִילּוּ הִיא שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת.
phrases.english: we view it as if it were made of metal.
phrases.notes: A result of רבי יהודה's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: רְחָבָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בְּרִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a strength requirement to the width rule of step 20 and records רבי יהודה's dissent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא requires the קורה to be both wide and strong. רבי יהודה requires only width, so straw or reeds are viewed as metal.

steps.title: Curved beams count as straight, round beams count as square
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a curved קורה is viewed as if it were straight, and a round קורה is viewed as if it were square.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the beam is curved, we look at it as if it were straight. If it is round, we look at it as if it were square.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its rules about the קורה over a מבוי. It now explains what to do when the beam is curved or round instead of flat and straight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אריח cannot really rest on a bent or rounded surface. The משנה still does not disqualify these beams. We picture the beam in a regular shape, so a curved beam counts as straight and a round beam counts as square, and then we check whether it has enough width.

keyTerms.meaning: We view it as if. We judge it by an imagined shape.

phrases.english: If it (the beam) is curved, we view it
phrases.notes: The subject is still the קורה from the earlier part of the משנה.

phrases.english: as if it were straight;
if it is round, we view it
as if it were square.
phrases.notes: The next line explains how a round beam's width is measured.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲקוּמָּה — רוֹאִין אוֹתָהּ כְּאִילּוּ הִיא פְּשׁוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rules on the קורה by applying the width requirement to beams with irregular shapes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A curved beam is judged as if it were straight, and a round beam is judged as if it were square.

steps.title: A circumference of three handbreadths gives a width of one handbreadth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a measuring rule for round beams: if the circumference is three טפחים, the beam counts as one טפח wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything whose circumference is three טפחים has a width of one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how to measure the round beam from the last line. It tells us how large around the beam must be to reach the required width of one טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot easily measure the width of a round beam directly, but you can measure around it. The משנה uses the rule that the distance around is three times the width across. So a beam that measures three טפחים around is one טפח wide and passes the requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: Circumference. The measurement all the way around.
Width (here, the distance straight across, the diameter)

steps.whatToRemember: The קורה must be one טפח wide. Unusual shapes do not disqualify it, because we picture a curved beam as straight and a round beam as square. A round beam qualifies when its circumference is three טפחים.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה is being careless with math. Saying "three times the width" is a rounded figure (the true number is a bit more than 3). The גמרא will discuss this, and also the question of whether a round beam must be large enough to hold a full square of one טפח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This three-to-one rule for circles is used in many places in ש"ס, such as סוכה, and it comes up again in the גמרא here.

phrases.english: Anything that has a circumference of three handbreadths
has a width of one handbreadth.
phrases.notes: Width here means the distance straight across the circle, its diameter.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּהֶיקֵּיפוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים יֵשׁ בּוֹ רוֹחַב טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the measuring rule for the round beam just discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A round beam with a circumference of three טפחים counts as one טפח wide.
